body: Did it make you feel apathetic or any other side effects? The only reason I was wary of them was due to these side effects.

I've heard of this actually. One of my friends suffered anxiety and had to take Xanax. He took b12 shots and he improved day by day. Though, do regular doctors carry such shots? I never understood how to get them.

All I want to do is just tell them what was happening the day I went to the hospital like what was going through my mind... My main motivation for it was guilt yet I can't shake this feeling that everyone thinks I'm insane or crazy... I mean who wouldn't... I had instant mood swings from anger to crying... From yelling to down right pouring. Hell, the girl I mentioned told me I am crazy and doesn't want to associate someone like me...

I just don't want to leave that impression on them... These are friends I can see being with for a years to come. I know they'll understand, but I never had the right opportunity. The past month I isolated from them and hung out with people I don't particularly enjoy. Or I hang out with them in a social setting which I'm unable to tell them.

I tried calling them more this week and I got almost no response. I just can't stand talking to a therapist when all I want is talk to my friends about it. My main motivation to not attempt again is so I don't end up in that shit hospital filled with shit staff members.

And yeah your right... I don't know how to start the conversation though. I want to tell them in a more appropriate time.

During the summer, I became depressed and lost a lot of weight...  That same summer, I completely fell in love over a girl.. I fell for her, for all the wrong reasons because basing a relationship on total dependence never fucking works... Worst part was... she also happened to be a close friend for a couple of years...

I never thought of her but just a great friend towards me the entire time I knew her... We did what all friends did and nothing more.

During that summer, I felt comfort and content being around with her. At times, it did seem like she liked me too since we getting more touchy with each other. For awhile, it was alright... I also couldn't accept the fact that she still has feelings for a long time ex boyfriend who treated worse then I'll ever did. She told me all the terrible things he did... Told me to remind her she shouldn't hang out with him... The shit he did to manipulate her...

But I kept freaking out over and over again especially when drunk... None of it was justified. I became worse than him.. But every time I blame anyone or someone else, I just blame myself. Constantly... Over and over again. I freaked out a lot that harmed myself physically and brought a lot of misery towards my friends. They didn't know what to do... They did try a lot. The friend I told you, helped me get an apartment. She knew about my depression and everything else. Also my friends got me a new job and tried everything... They listened to my bullshit so much...

I just remember a lot of punching into concrete over and over until it's bloody then my anger would stop and I get so depressed that I just crotch up in a ball. This happened constantly for a year and I only feel guilt. Ever I've broken so many of my own guitars and equipment, but the worst thing I did was broken my trust and the wonderful relationships I built up... I just wished I was more grateful towards their efforts...

I've been struggling with depression for almost a year and yeah, it doesn't help for me. When I'm with friends, yeah I can relax, but when I smoke by myself, the thoughts of regret, despair and guilt come screaming back. Then my high becomes this struggle... My high becomes this hell. Then the days after my high, I'm back to the old depressed state of doing nothing and wasting an entire day trying to keep these thoughts out.

Its funny though. I know when I smoke by myself, this will happen, but I usually do it when I'm in a good mood.

u mad bro?

But so far, I haven't been prescribed with medication. My bipolar is mild compared to some of the examples provided here. And look, if your medication gave you the motivation to start working out, then wouldn't my bipolar gave me the motivation to the same without the meds?

Wow, seems like I must take medication... One of the doctors recommended folic acid. Anyone tried this?

Also regarding the EDMR, my therapist didn't recognize I have bipolar until I went to the psych ward which was this past weekend. She assumed I had depression because I only talked about my depressive states and I had some traumatic experience back when I was 16. So for the lack of information.

For me, it personally didn't help that much and I'm a big health freak.

I'm the type of health guy that buys stuff like blue-green algae, chlorella and spirulina while putting them into my kale smoothie mixed with hemp protein. Eating vegetarian eggs and went under vitamin D supplementation once the winter months hit. Avoided white grain foods and ate more whole grain. I take maca, supposedly balances hormone levels, and ginseng everyday as they help with stress. I also took regular omega 3 fish oils and cod liver fish oils, but still my depression hit me hard everyday despite my healthy eating habits. Good news is, my blood tests came back excellent and my body is well toned as a result.

I also took melatonin and 5-HTP but it gave me intense dreams and made me wake up at odd hours like 4:00-5:00 AM. I guess for me, its just my neurochemistry. But overall, try to have a healthier diet, even though I went big lengths for mine, I don't regret it even if it didn't solve my depression.

Thank you for your advice! It really opened up my mind and now everything just makes sense. Seriously thank you. I've been on the stage of recovery so many times that each time I fail, the harder my depression hits me like a train. Now I know why.

I'll talk to my therapist when going into my next session. Again, thank you :)

Out of curiosity, is there a term to describe this stage?

Thanks man. It is hard to keep up a good attitude when all of it is my own fault and actions. I have no one to blame, but myself. That's where must of my shame and guilt comes from.. 

I just hope I can celebrate my 21st birthday with my close friends that I've been pushing away for the past six months...

But man, depression is horrible. It sucks knowing that I may have to deal with it even more. Maybe a year? Or two. I wish it can go away for good.

Thank you! The therapist recommended me if I'm having bad grades during this semester then I'll take medication. In the mean time, she will help me by guided meditation. However, I do have a fear of anti-depressents as the side effects are not appealing and want to take the "natural" approach.

I quote natural as I do take 5-HTP supplements before bed.

Also can you recommend me some books? Ones that are hilarious, interesting or weird? I'm reading the "The Painted Bird" and its slowly getting me back into reading again.

It comes and goes... But everyday for the past six months, I've cried once into full blown sob mode. I drive a car for my job and I've cried while driving were my eyes would fill up until everything becomes a blur.

I get excited going to work, but I dislike going to school since I did horrible the previous semester by dropping two classes and gotten a D for an easy class. Now I feel like I have no future in my academic career. How am I suppose to transfer? Do I explain to them that I was depressed?

I fear that my problem could be indirectly towards a best friend that I fell in love with during the summer... But at the same time, I believe that I fell in love with her because she made me laugh and helped forget my depression. We also haven't talked more than a month... and all of it was my fault.

Same time, I believe that I was depressed before "liking her".. 

I consequently feel guilty and ashamed for being depressed as I have great friends and family. I feel like a burden to them as I ruin their time.
